text: Defender for Endpoint's core ideas don't change under Defender XDR — a device still has to be onboarded before its sensor reports anything, and automated investigation and remediation still reaches the same verdicts the same way. What changes is where that telemetry goes next, and who else gets to see it.

Onboarding still registers a device with the tenant before it reports. Alerts are still raised by the same endpoint sensor covered earlier in this path. Automated investigation and remediation still investigates a file or process tree, reaches a verdict, and remediates high-confidence malicious cases automatically — none of that machinery changed.

What's different is evaluation scope. Before Defender XDR, an endpoint alert was judged only against other endpoint alerts. Under Defender XDR, it's judged against Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps signal too — so an alert that looked minor on its own can turn out to be one step in a larger, multi-product incident.

Microsoft Sentinel has a real data connector for Defender XDR, listed historically under its earlier name, Microsoft 365 Defender. It brings in two things: the already-correlated Defender XDR incidents, and the raw Advanced Hunting tables behind them — real tables like DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceNetworkEvents, DeviceLogonEvents, AlertInfo, and AlertEvidence.

Defender XDR's own portal already unifies its four workloads. The reason to also connect it to Sentinel is scope — Sentinel sees data Defender XDR never will, like a firewall's logs, a VPN concentrator's logs, or a non-Microsoft SaaS audit log, all inside the same workspace.

Once that connector is enabled, an analyst can write one KQL query joining DeviceLogonEvents against a VPN log table to check whether a suspicious endpoint sign-in matches a legitimate remote session. That cross-source correlation is something neither Defender XDR nor Sentinel can do alone, and it's a pattern this course returns to once Chapter 6 covers real incident investigation.
